The twelve cars

You are welcome to come and view the cars before you decide. One of the reviews above is from a couple who did exactly that.

Vintage Rolls Royce

1938 Phantom II

Coach built, and the largest Rolls Royce produced. Plenty of space for the largest ball gown or wedding dress. Ivory leather interior, with two additional adult fold-away occasional seats.

Up to 7 passengers

Vintage Rolls Royce

1937 Phantom III

Black over white paintwork. The interior is in dusky pink cloth with matching carpets and an ornate headlining, with two additional adult fold-away occasional seats.

Up to 6 passengers

Vintage Rolls Royce

1933 Phantom II

A striking colour combination of navy and ivory paintwork with an ivory leather interior. Plus two fold-down adult occasional seats.

Up to 6 passengers

Vintage style

Imperial Viscount Landaulette

A vintage-style car in ivory paintwork with a matching cream leather interior. The soft top lowers in seconds, so it can be open or closed depending on the weather on the day.

Up to 7 passengers

Latest addition

Imperial Viscount Landaulette

Ivory and silver paintwork with an ivory leather interior. The soft top lowers in seconds.

Up to 7 passengers

Vintage style

Ford Bramwith

Ivory and black coachwork with a cream leather interior, seating up to seven in a conference arrangement so everyone faces each other. Ample leg room, and room for the bride’s dress.

Up to 7 passengers

Three cars

The Daimler limousines

Three elegant Daimlers: two in ivory, and one in black and Old English White. Each has two occasional seats. They are the usual choice for bridesmaids, mothers and guests, and they match well alongside any of the vintage cars.

7 passengers plus the driver, per car
